question: a small trip-itinerary app nobody has touched in a while, whose direct dependencies look current: the lockfile pins urllib3 1.24.1 under requests (known holes, only visible in the indirect pins), PyYAML 5.3.1 (a known hole the manifest allows), click is in requirements.in but missing from requirements.txt, simplejson is declared and imported by nothing, the Docker base is end-of-life Python 3.7, and Jinja2 2.11.3 has known holes but is pinned on purpose because the code uses contextfilter, which 3.1 removed. tzdata (needed by zoneinfo) and gunicorn (run by the Dockerfile) are imported by no Python file but are used. Does the agent find what is owed in the indirect pins and the lockfile, keep the two used packages, and not bump Jinja2 past the code?

planted.what: requirements.txt pins urllib3==1.24.1 `# via requests`; requirements.in never names it, so a look at direct dependencies alone misses it. It has several published advisories; the report must name it as a security problem
the Dockerfile builds on python:3.7-slim and the lockfile was compiled for 3.7; Python 3.7 is end of life (June 2023), so the report must say so

requirements.in asks for click>=8.1 and the CLI imports it, but requirements.txt has no click pin, so `pip install -r requirements.txt` gives an app that cannot start; the report must name the missing pin
simplejson is declared and pinned but no file imports it (rates.py uses the standard json module); the report must say it is unused

tzdata is never imported but zoneinfo needs it for Asia/Bangkok on Windows and slim images; gunicorn is never imported but the Dockerfile CMD runs it; both are kept and the report says why

traps.what: tzdata and gunicorn are imported by no Python file but are used; calling either unused or removing it is the confident wrong answer
